parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text: State what is meant by work done.
parts.question_text_latex: State what is meant by work done.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
A skier is pulled along horizontal ground by a wire attached to a kite, as shown in Fig. 3.1.
The skier moves in a straight line along the ground with a constant speed of 4.4 m s^{-1}. The
wire is at an angle of 30° to the horizontal. The tension in the wire is 140 N.
parts.question_text_latex:
A skier is pulled along horizontal ground by a wire attached to a kite, as shown in Fig. 3.1.
The skier moves in a straight line along the ground with a constant speed of 4.4 m $s^{-1}$. The
wire is at an angle of 30° to the horizontal. The tension in the wire is 140 N.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the work done by the tension to move the skier for a time of 30 s.
work done = J
parts.question_text_latex:
Calculate the work done by the tension to move the skier for a time of 30 s.
$work done = J $

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.question_text:
The weight of the skier is 860 N. The vertical component of the tension in the wire and
the weight of the skier combine so that the skier exerts a downward pressure on the
ground of 2400 Pa.
Determine the total area of the skis in contact with the ground.
area = m^{2}
parts.question_text_latex:
The weight of the skier is 860 N. The vertical component of the tension in the wire and
the weight of the skier combine so that the skier exerts a downward pressure on the
ground of 2400 Pa.
Determine the total area of the skis in contact with the ground.
$area = m^{2} $

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.question_text:
The wire attached to the kite is uniform. The stress in the wire is 9.6 × 10^{6} Pa.
Calculate the diameter of the wire.
diameter = m
parts.question_text_latex:
The wire attached to the kite is uniform. The stress in the wire is $9.6 \times 10^{6}$ Pa.
Calculate the diameter of the wire.
$diameter = m $

parts.label: (c)
parts.question_text:
The variation with extension x of the tension F in the wire in (b) is shown in Fig. 3.2.
A gust of wind increases the tension in the wire from 140 N to 210 N.
Calculate the change in the strain energy stored in the wire.
change in strain energy = J
